definitions.gloss: cheerful-looking; merry; seeming to enjoy oneself
definitions.explanation: Appearing to be having fun or enjoying oneself, as seen from outside. Mostly used in narration and descriptions.

examples.japanese: {楽|たの}しげ⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{歌|うた}う→歌う：00684_utau⟧。
⟦{子供|こども}→子供：00554_kodomo⟧たち⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{楽|たの}しげな⟦{声|こえ}→声：02207_koe⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{聞|き}こえる→聞こえる：01229_kikoeru⟧。
examples.english: I can hear the children's happy voices.

examples.japanese: ⟦{公園|こうえん}→公園：00581_kouen⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{家族連|かぞくづ}れ→家族連れ：31691_kazokuzure⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{楽|たの}しげ⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦お{弁当|べんとう}→お弁当：02864_obentou⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{広|ひろ}げていた→広げる：01981_hirogeru⟧。
examples.english: In the park, families were happily spreading out their packed lunches.

notes:
FORMS:
- {楽|たの}しげな + noun: cheerful ~ ({楽|たの}しげな⟦{笑|わら}い{声|ごえ}→笑い声：24414_waraigoe⟧)
- {楽|たの}しげ⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧ + verb: merrily, happily

USAGE:
げ after an adjective stem means 'with an air of ~': it describes how others look, not how you feel. In conversation, {楽|たの}しそう is the usual word; {楽|たの}しげ sounds written or literary.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {楽|たの}しそう: looks like fun, seems to be enjoying it; the everyday equivalent
- {悲|かな}しげ: sad-looking; the opposite, formed the same way
